content: 1. Administer diazepam rectally to prevent drug expulsion. If convulsions recur, administer an additional 10 mg dose. For maintenance, provide 10 mg (2 ml) every hour during transport. Diazepam is available in vials containing 10 mg in 2 ml for IV or rectal use. The initial dose is 10 mg (2 ml), and a second dose of 10 mg (2 ml) can be given if necessary. 2. If the diastolic blood pressure exceeds 110 mmHg, administer hydralazine 5 mg IV slowly over 3–4 minutes. If IV administration is not possible, administer the drug intramuscularly. If the diastolic blood pressure remains above 90 mmHg, repeat the dose at 30-minute intervals until the diastolic pressure is approximately 90 mmHg. 3. For infections, administer appropriate IV or IM antibiotics. Ensure the first dose of antibiotics is given before referral. If referral is delayed or not possible, continue antibiotics for 48 hours after the woman becomes fever-free. If symptoms persist or the woman experiences postpartum weakness or abdominal pain, refer her urgently to a hospital. 4. For uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria during pregnancy, confirm the diagnosis parasitologically if there is clinical suspicion based on fever or a history of fever. In the first trimester, treat with quinine and clindamycin for 7 days. Quinine should be prepared as a 2 ml vial containing 300 mg/ml. Administer a loading dose of 20 mg/kg (assuming a weight of 50–60 kg), followed by 10 mg/kg every 8 hours if referral is not possible. Dilute the required dosage in IV 5% glucose solution to correct hypoglycemia. Administer oral quinine and clindamycin once the patient can tolerate tablets to complete the 7-day course. In the second and third trimesters, use artesunate. Prepare a 1 ml vial containing 60 mg/ml and a 1 ml vial of 5% bicarbonate solution. Administer 4 mg/kg IM or IV at 0, 12, and 24 hours, then once daily until oral artesunate (2 mg/kg/day) can be taken to complete a 7-day course. 5. In cases of vaginal bleeding during early pregnancy or post-abortion care, assess the woman thoroughly. Ask about the onset, amount, and progression of bleeding, as well as any history of pregnancy, missed periods, or recent abortion attempts. Check for symptoms such as fainting, abdominal pain, or fever. Examine for the amount of bleeding, foul-smelling vaginal discharge, lower abdominal pain, fever, pallor, and pulse rate. 6. For complicated abortion with signs such as foul-smelling discharge, uterine manipulation, abdominal pain, or fever above 38°C, insert an IV line and administer fluids. Provide pain relief with paracetamol and administer appropriate IM or IV antibiotics. Refer the woman urgently to a hospital. 7. For threatened abortion with light vaginal bleeding, observe the bleeding for 4–6 hours. If there is no decrease or if bleeding worsens, refer the woman to a hospital. If the bleeding decreases, allow the woman to go home but advise her to return immediately if bleeding increases. Follow up in 2 days. 8. For complete abortion with a history of heavy bleeding that is now decreasing or absent, check preventive measures, advise on self-care, and counsel on family planning. Advise the woman to return if bleeding does not stop within 2 days. 9. For ectopic pregnancy with symptoms such as abdominal pain, fainting, pallor, or weakness, insert an IV line, administer fluids, and refer the woman urgently to a hospital. 10. Provide tetanus toxoid if due, and supply 3 months of iron supplementation with counseling on compliance. Check the woman’s HIV status. If unknown, counsel on HIV testing. If HIV-positive, refer to HIV services for further assessment and treatment, provide support, and counsel on opportunistic infections, safer sex practices, and condom use. If HIV-negative, reinforce safer sex practices and condom use. 11. If the woman tests positive for syphilis (RPR-positive), treat with benzathine penicillin and advise on treating her partner. Encourage HIV testing and counseling, and reinforce condom use. 12. Advise on self-care after abortion, including rest, hygiene (changing pads every 4–6 hours, daily perineal washing), and avoiding sexual relations until bleeding stops. Instruct the woman to return immediately if she experiences increased bleeding, foul-smelling discharge, abdominal pain, fever, weakness, dizziness, or fainting. Advise her to return if menstruation does not resume within 6 weeks. 13. Counsel on family planning, explaining that pregnancy can occur soon after abortion if contraception is not used. Any family planning method can be initiated immediately after an uncomplicated first-trimester abortion. Delay IUD insertion or sterilization if there is an infection or injury until healing occurs. Arrange for the woman to see a family planning counselor or provide direct counseling. 14. Provide emotional support after abortion, allowing the woman to discuss her concerns and health. Facilitate family and community support if she is interested, and educate them on how to assist her. Inform them about the risks of post-abortion complications and the importance of seeking medical help if danger signs occur. Encourage family planning if another pregnancy is not desired. 15. During follow-up visits, reassure women with threatened abortion if bleeding has stopped, and provide antenatal care. If bleeding continues, assess and manage as per early pregnancy bleeding or post-abortion care guidelines. Administer the first dose of appropriate IV/IM antibiotics if there are signs of infection, such as fever, foul-smelling discharge, or abdominal pain.
